Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters Scott Murray Tue 17 Nov 2026 13.54 EST First published on Tue 17 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 53m ago The teams 
 1h ago Preamble 
 35m ago 13.52 EST Portugal make four changes after that 4-1 defeat at home to Denmark. Rúben Dias is suspended so António Silva comes into the defence. João Neves, João Cancelo and Francisco Trincão step up; João Félix, Alberto Costa and Rúben Neves sit down. The Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs is also on the bench, sporting Portugal’s fancy new post-Cristiano continental-style No 7.
 Portugal immortalise Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt in tribute to national legend Read more Share 46m ago 13.42 EST Wales make six changes to their starting line-up following the 3-1 defeat in Norway. Two are enforced: Ethan Ampadu is suspended while Neco Williams is injured. In come Danny Ward, David Brooks, Connor Roberts, Rubin Colwill, Sorba Thomas and Josh Sheehan. Karl Darlow, Liam Cullen, Lewis Koumas and Brennan Johnson drop to the bench.
 Norway 3-1 Wales: Nations League – as it happened Read more Share 53m ago 13.34 EST The teams
 Wales: Ward, Roberts, Rodon, B Davies, Dasilva, Wilson, Sheehan, Brooks, D James, R Colwill, Thomas.
 Portugal: Costa, Dalot, Silva, Veiga, Cancelo, Vitinha, Fernandes, Neto, Trincao, Ramos, Neves.
 Referee: Sven Jablonski (Germany) 
 Share Updated at  13.54 EST 1h ago 13.30 EST Preamble
 This is a free hit for Wales . Craig Bellamy and his men have nothing to worry about, because despite being guaranteed to finish bottom of Group A4, as a result of the old head-to-head rule …
 1. Portugal P5 W4 D0 L1 GD+2 Pts 12
2. Denmark P5 W3 D0 L2 GD+3 Pts 9
3. Norway P5 W2 D0 L3 GD0 Pts 6
4. Wales P5 W1 D0 L4 GD-5 Pts 3 
 … they’re also guaranteed to finish top of the ranking of League A’s fourth-placed teams …
 1. Wales (A4) P5 W1 D0 L4 GD-5 Pts 3
2. Serbia (A2) P6 W0 D0 L6 GD-8 Pts 0
3. Turkey (A1) P6 W0 D0 L6 GD-11 Pts 0
4. Czechia (A3) P6 W0 D0 L6 GD-11 Pts 0 
 … and so this Byzantine journey will lead them to a relegation/promotion play-off with some of the runners-up in League B. But that’s a concern for March; this is now! Can Wales bounce back after their spirited defeat in Norway ? Will Portugal prove a point after their humbling by Denmark , the first misstep in the post-Him world? Kick-off is at 7.45pm. It’s on!
